mainTopic: Humility, רבי's suffering, rescuing others' children for תורה, and keeping תורה in the family
overview: The גמרא finishes רבי's list of humble people. It doubts the examples of יונתן and the בני בתירה, and concludes that רבן שמעון בן גמליאל was surely humble. רבי then takes on thirteen years of painful suffering. The suffering began when he showed no mercy to a calf, and it ended when he showed mercy to baby weasels. רבי rescues the wayward son of רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, who grows into the scholar רבי יוסי. A בת קול later explains why he could not be buried beside his father. רבי also brings רבי טרפון's grandson to תשובה, and the גמרא explains why he worked so hard: teaching someone else's child תורה brings enormous reward. Next comes a promise that three generations of תלמידי חכמים keep תורה in a family forever, shown through the fasts of רב יוסף and רבי זירא. The amud ends as רב begins explaining the פסוק about why the land was destroyed, and his answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The three humble people and how each showed it
steps.stepSummary: רבי's list of three humble people ends with the בני בתירה and יונתן בן שאול, and the גמרא explains the humble act of each one.
steps.simpleTranslation: The three humble people were my father, the sons of Beteira, and Yonatan son of Shaul. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל: we just saw it, when he called himself a fox. The בני בתירה stepped down and made הלל the נשיא over them. יונתן told דוד, 'You will be king and I will be second to you.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes a list of three humble people and then explains, one by one, what each of them did that showed humility.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each person gave up honor that he could have kept. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל called himself small. The בני בתירה gave up the position of נשיא. יונתן, the king's son, gave up his claim to the throne.

keyTerms.meaning: The sons of Beteira, leaders before הלל
The head of the Jewish leadership and the סנהדרין

phrases.english: and the sons of Beteira, and Yonatan son of Shaul.

phrases.aramaic: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל – הָא דַּאֲמַרַן:
phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel: that which we just said.
phrases.notes: This points back to the story just told, where he humbly called himself a fox.

phrases.english: The sons of Beteira: as the Master said,
they seated him [Hillel] at the head and appointed him Nasi over them.

phrases.aramaic: יוֹנָתָן בֶּן שָׁאוּל, דְּקָאָמַר לֵיהּ לְדָוִד:
phrases.english: Yonatan son of Shaul: as he said to David,
"And you will be king over Israel,
and I will be second to you."
phrases.notes: שמואל א 23:17

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל – הָא דַּאֲמַרַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes and explains the list of humble people that began just before this text.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Three people showed humility: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, the בני בתירה, and יונתן בן שאול.

steps.title: Maybe the בני בתירה and יונתן had no real choice
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the proof for two of the three: maybe they gave up power because they had to, not because they were humble.
steps.simpleTranslation: How do we know they were humble? Maybe יונתן saw that everyone was following דוד anyway. And maybe the בני בתירה saw that הלל was simply greater than them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions whether the stories about יונתן and the בני בתירה really prove humility.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Giving up a position only counts as humility if you could have kept it. If the people were already behind דוד, or הלל was clearly the greater scholar, stepping aside may have been plain realism rather than humility.
steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying they were proud. It only says their actions do not clearly prove humility.

phrases.english: From where [do we know this]?
Perhaps Yonatan son of Shaul
[gave in] because he saw that the world was drawn after David;
the sons of Beteira also
[stepped down] because they saw that Hillel was greater than them.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִמַּאי? דִּלְמָא יוֹנָתָן בֶּן שָׁאוּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the proofs given in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that יונתן and the בני בתירה acted from humility.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Their actions can be explained by outside pressure or realism, so they do not prove humility.

steps.title: Only רבן שמעון בן גמליאל was surely humble
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that, at least, רבן שמעון בן גמליאל was definitely humble.
steps.simpleTranslation: But רבן שמעון בן גמליאל was certainly humble.
steps.whatsHappening: After doubting two of the three examples, the גמרא states the one example that holds up for sure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing forced רבן שמעון בן גמליאל to call himself a fox. He was the נשיא and lost nothing by keeping his honor, so his self-lowering can only come from real humility.
steps.whatToRemember: True humility means lowering yourself when nothing forces you to. That is why only רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's example stands without doubt.

phrases.english: But Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel
certainly was humble.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל וַדַּאי עִנְוְותָן הֲוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Concedes the challenge for two examples and holds on to the third.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל was certainly humble, even if the other two examples can be doubted.

steps.title: רבי accepts thirteen years of suffering
steps.stepSummary: רבי decides that suffering is precious and takes on thirteen years of painful illness. There are two versions of how those years were divided.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי said: suffering is precious. He accepted thirteen years of it: six with kidney stones and seven with scurvy. Some say seven with kidney stones and six with scurvy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the earlier story about רבי, who now chooses to take suffering upon himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי learned from the earlier story that suffering brings greatness, so he accepted it on purpose. The two versions agree on the total of thirteen years and argue only about how they were split.

phrases.english: Rebbi said: Sufferings are precious.
He accepted upon himself thirteen years [of suffering]:
six with kidney stones,
and seven with scurvy.
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets; the corrected wording is the word in square brackets.

phrases.english: And some say: seven with kidney stones,
and six with scurvy.
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the word in round brackets.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי, חֲבִיבִין יִסּוּרִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of humility and returns to the story of רבי and suffering.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Suffering is precious. רבי accepted thirteen years of it.

steps.title: Even the roar of the animals could not drown out רבי's cries
steps.stepSummary: רבי's stableman was richer than a king. His herd's noise was huge, yet רבי's cries of pain were louder and reached sailors at sea.
steps.simpleTranslation: The stableman in רבי's house was richer than King Shapur. When he fed the animals, their noise carried three מיל. He would time the feeding for when רבי went into the bathroom, but even so רבי's voice rose above theirs, and sailors at sea heard him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story showing how intense רבי's suffering was.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story builds up how loud the animals were: a herd so large that even its keeper was rich, and noise heard three מיל away. That makes the ending stronger: רבי's cries were louder still.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי chose his suffering, and it was real and terrible. Even the noise of his huge herd could not hide his cries.

phrases.english: The stableman of Rebbi's house
was richer than King Shapur.
When he would throw feed to the animals,
the sound would travel three mil.
He would make sure to throw [it] at that very time
when Rebbi went into the bathroom,
and even so, his voice rose above their sound,
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the letter מ in round brackets. The meaning stays the same.

phrases.english: and the sailors at sea heard him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַהוּרְיָירֵיהּ דְּבֵי רַבִּי הֲוָה עַתִּיר מִשַּׁבּוּר מַלְכָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows how severe the suffering that רבי accepted in step 4 really was.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי's cries of pain were louder than the noise of his huge herd.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר's suffering was on a higher level than רבי's
steps.stepSummary: The suffering of רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון was greater than רבי's, because his came and left out of love, while רבי's came and left because of specific incidents.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even so, the sufferings of רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון were greater than those of רבי. His came out of love and left out of love, while רבי's came because of an incident and left because of an incident.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא compares רבי's suffering with the suffering of רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון and says the second was on a higher level.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Right after describing how intense רבי's suffering was, the גמרא adds that רבי אלעזר's was still more special. The reason is how it started and ended: רבי אלעזר's was purely יסורין של אהבה, while רבי's was tied to things he did. This sets up the next steps, which tell those two incidents.

keyTerms.meaning: Because of an incident, something that happened

phrases.english: But even so,
the sufferings of Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon
were greater than those of Rabbi.
For whereas Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon's sufferings
came out of love and left out of love,
Rabbi's came because of an incident
and left because of an incident.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַאֲפִילּוּ הָכִי, יִסּוּרֵי דְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן עֲדִיפִי מִדְּרַבִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the description of רבי's suffering by comparing it to רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון's suffering.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Suffering that comes purely out of love is on a higher level than suffering caused by one's own actions.

steps.title: What was the incident that brought רבי's suffering?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the incident was that caused רבי's suffering to begin.
steps.simpleTranslation: "They came because of an incident": what was it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short question to set up the story that comes next: what event caused רבי's suffering?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 6 only said that רבי's suffering came "because of an incident" without saying what happened. Here the גמרא asks for the details, and the next step answers.

keyTerms.meaning: What is it? What does it refer to?

phrases.aramaic: עַל יְדֵי מַעֲשֶׂה בָּאוּ מַאי הִיא –
phrases.english: "They came because of an incident": what was it?

steps.triggerLanguage: עַל יְדֵי מַעֲשֶׂה בָּאוּ מַאי הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the details of the first incident mentioned in step 6.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What event caused רבי's suffering to begin.

steps.title: The calf that ran to רבי before slaughter
steps.stepSummary: A calf being led to slaughter hid its head in רבי's garment and cried. רבי told it to go, since it was created for this. Heaven decided that since he did not show mercy, suffering should come upon him.
steps.simpleTranslation: A calf was being led to slaughter. It went and hung its head in the corner of רבי's garment and cried. He said to it: "Go, this is what you were created for." In Heaven they said: "Since he does not show mercy, let suffering come upon him."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by telling the story of the calf that brought suffering on רבי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: What רבי said was true: the animal was created to be eaten. Still, Heaven judged him for not showing compassion to a frightened creature that came to him for help. The punishment, suffering, fits the failing, a lack of mercy.

phrases.english: There was a certain calf
that they were leading to slaughter.
It went and hung its head
in the corner of Rabbi's garment and was crying.
He said to it: Go, for this you were created.
They said: Since he does not show mercy,
phrases.notes: "They" here means in Heaven.

phrases.english: let sufferings come upon him.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּהָהוּא עִגְלָא דַּהֲווֹ קָא מַמְטוּ לֵיהּ לִשְׁחִיטָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question of step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי's suffering began because he did not show mercy to a calf that came to him crying before slaughter.

steps.title: The baby weasels רבי protected
steps.stepSummary: רבי's maidservant was sweeping baby weasels out of the house. רבי told her to leave them, quoting "His mercies are on all His works." Heaven decided that since he showed mercy, they would show mercy to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: "And they left because of an incident": One day רבי's maidservant was sweeping the house. Baby weasels were lying there, and she was sweeping them out. He said to her: "Leave them alone. It is written: 'And His mercies are on all His works.'" In Heaven they said: "Since he shows mercy, we will have mercy on him."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now explains the second incident, the one that made רבי's suffering go away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This story is the mirror image of the calf story. There, רבי did not show mercy, and suffering came. Here he showed mercy to small creatures, and Heaven answered with mercy and ended his suffering.

keyTerms.meaning: We will have mercy on him

steps.whatToRemember: רבי's suffering began when he failed to show mercy to an animal and ended when he showed mercy to animals. Heaven treats a person the way he treats others.

phrases.english: And "they left because of an incident":

phrases.aramaic: יוֹמָא חַד הֲוָה קָא כָנְשָׁא אַמְּתֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי בֵּיתָא,
phrases.english: One day, Rabbi's maidservant was sweeping the house.
Some baby weasels were lying there,
and she was sweeping them out.
He said to her: Leave them alone,
as it is written: "And His mercies are on all His works."
phrases.notes: תהלים 145:9

phrases.english: They said: Since he shows mercy,
we will have mercy on him.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעַל יְדֵי מַעֲשֶׂה הָלְכוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the second half of step 6, how רבי's suffering ended, as a mirror of the calf story.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי's suffering ended because he showed mercy to baby weasels, so Heaven showed mercy to him.

steps.title: The blessings in the world during their years of suffering
steps.stepSummary: During רבי אלעזר's years of suffering, no one died before their time. During רבי's years of suffering, the world did not need rain.
steps.simpleTranslation: During all the years of רבי אלעזר's suffering, no person died before his time. During all the years of רבי's suffering, the world did not need rain.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells us what good came to the world while each of these sages was suffering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The suffering of a great צדיק is not only personal; it brings blessing to everyone. For רבי אלעזר, nobody died early. For רבי, the world was spared the need for rain, which the next step explains is a real blessing.

phrases.english: All the years of Rabbi Elazar's suffering,
no person died before his time.
All the years of Rabbi's suffering,
the world did not need rain.

steps.triggerLanguage: כּוּלְּהוּ שְׁנֵי יִסּוּרֵי דְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר לָא שָׁכֵיב אִינִישׁ בְּלָא זִמְנֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to comparing the two sages, now by the blessings their suffering brought.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each sage's suffering brought a blessing to the world: no early deaths for רבי אלעזר, and no need for rain for רבי.

steps.title: Why not needing rain is a blessing
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר רב שילא says a rainy day is as hard as a day of judgment, and אמימר says that if rain were not needed, the Rabbis would pray to cancel it.
steps.simpleTranslation: For רבה בר רב שילא said: A day of rain is as hard as a day of judgment. And אמימר said: If the world did not need it, the Rabbis would pray for mercy about it and cancel it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings two sayings to show why a world without a need for rain is a blessing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone might think no rain sounds like a drought, a curse. These two sayings show that rain itself is hard on people, and we only want it because we need it. So not needing rain at all is a real gift.
steps.confusionAlert: "No rain" here is not a drought. The world simply did not need rain, as the next step shows the ground was still full of water.

phrases.english: For Rabba bar Rav Sheila said:
A day of rain is as hard as a day of judgment.
And Ameimar said:
If it were not needed by the world,

phrases.aramaic: בָּעוּ רַבָּנַן רַחֲמֵי עֲלֵיהּ וּמְבַטְּלִי לֵיהּ.
phrases.english: the Rabbis would pray for mercy about it and cancel it.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַבָּה בַּר רַב שֵׁילָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 10's claim that not needing rain was a blessing.
steps.raayaObject: That the world not needing rain during רבי's suffering was a blessing.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The sayings of רבה בר רב שילא and אמימר about how hard rain is on people.

steps.title: The ground stayed full of water anyway
steps.stepSummary: Even without rain, when a radish was pulled from the ground, the hole it left was filled with water.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even so, when they would pull a radish out of its row, the hole left behind would be full of water.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes by showing that even with no rain, the earth was still very moist.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This shows the blessing was complete: the world got all the benefit of rain without the hardship of rainy days. The ground was so wet that pulling up one radish left a hole full of water.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי's suffering brought a world that had plenty of water without the trouble of rain, and רבי אלעזר's suffering kept people from dying early.

phrases.english: Even so,
when they would pull up a radish from its row,
there would remain a hole full of water.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲפִילּוּ הָכִי, כִּי הֲווֹ עָקְרִי פּוּגְלָא מִמֵּשָׁרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes step 10 by showing the world still had plenty of water without rain.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even without rain, the earth stayed so moist that a pulled-up radish left a hole full of water.

steps.title: רבי asks whether the righteous man left a son
steps.stepSummary: רבי comes to the town of רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון and asks the people whether that צדיק has a son.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי came to the place where רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון had lived. He asked the people: Does that righteous man have a son?
steps.whatsHappening: A new story starts. רבי visits רבי אלעזר's town and asks if he left a son, setting up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier steps compared the suffering of רבי and רבי אלעזר. Now רבי, who admired רבי אלעזר, wants to know whether his legacy continues through a child.

keyTerms.meaning: Happened to come to, arrived at

phrases.english: Rabbi happened to come to the place
of Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon.
He said to them:
Does that righteous man have a son?
phrases.notes: "That righteous man" is רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, who had already passed away.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיקְּלַע רַבִּי לְאַתְרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the stories about רבי and רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון with a new episode about רבי אלעזר's son.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון left a son behind.

steps.title: The son has gone badly astray
steps.stepSummary: The townspeople answer that he has a son, but he has fallen into a sinful life.
steps.simpleTranslation: They told him: He has a son. And any harlot who is hired for two coins hires him for eight.
steps.whatsHappening: The people answer רבי's question: yes, there is a son, but he is living an immoral life.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer is sharp: the son of such a great צדיק is so far gone that harlots pay him more than they themselves are paid. This sets up how low he starts, so his later greatness will stand out.

phrases.english: They said to him: He has a son.
And any harlot who is hired for two
hires him for eight.
phrases.notes: This is their pointed way of telling רבי that the son has gone completely off the path.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: יֵשׁ לוֹ בֵּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי's question from step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes, there is a son, but he is living a sinful life.

steps.title: רבי gives the son סמיכה and sends him to his uncle
steps.stepSummary: רבי brings the son back, ordains him with the title רבי, and gives him to his maternal uncle רבי שמעון בן איסי בן לקוניא to learn.
steps.simpleTranslation: He brought him, ordained him as רבי, and handed him over to רבי שמעון בן איסי בן לקוניא, his mother's brother.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי acts to rescue the boy: he takes him, gives him סמיכה, and puts him in his uncle's care.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי gives him the honor of the title before he has earned it, hoping it will pull him upward. He chooses a family member, the boy's uncle, to be his teacher.

keyTerms.meaning: He ordained him, gave him סמיכה

phrases.english: He brought him, ordained him as "Rabbi,"

phrases.aramaic: וְאַשְׁלְמֵיהּ לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אִיסִי בֶּן לָקוֹנְיָא
phrases.english: and handed him over to Rabbi Shimon ben Isi ben Lakonya,
his mother's brother.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַתְיֵיהּ, אַסְמְכֵיהּ בְּרַבִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי reacts to the bad news of step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי rescues the boy by ordaining him and placing him with his uncle to learn תורה.

steps.title: The boy keeps wanting to go home
steps.stepSummary: Every day the boy says he is going back to his town.
steps.simpleTranslation: Every day he would say: I am going back to my town.
steps.whatsHappening: The boy finds the learning hard and keeps threatening to leave. This sets up his uncle's response in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rescue is not instant. The boy's old life still pulls at him, and the story shows the struggle before the change.

phrases.english: Every day he would say:
I am going to my town.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֹּל יוֹמָא הֲוָה אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows how the boy reacted to being placed with his uncle.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The boy repeatedly wants to abandon his learning and return home.

steps.title: The uncle rebukes him: look at the honor you were given
steps.stepSummary: The uncle challenges him: you were made a scholar, wrapped in a golden cloak, and called רבי, and you want to go home?
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: They made you wise, spread a golden cloak over you, and call you רבי, and you say, I am going to my town!
steps.whatsHappening: The uncle pushes back hard against the boy's wish to leave, reminding him of the honor he has already received.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The uncle uses the honor רבי gave him as a reason to live up to it. The question is not really asking anything; it is a rebuke meant to shame him into staying.

phrases.english: He said to him: They have made you wise,
and spread a golden cloak over you,
and they call you "Rabbi,"
and you say, "I am going to my town"!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: חַכִּים עָבְדוּ יָתָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the boy's daily wish to leave in step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: The boy's plan to leave his learning and go home.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Someone who has been honored as a scholar and called רבי cannot simply walk away from it.

steps.title: The boy swears to drop the idea of leaving
steps.stepSummary: The boy answers with an oath that he has abandoned the thought of going home.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I swear, this idea is abandoned.
steps.whatsHappening: The boy accepts his uncle's rebuke and commits to stay and learn.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the turning point of the story. The uncle's push works, and the boy decides to stay.

phrases.english: He said to him: I swear, this is abandoned.
phrases.notes: He means he is giving up the idea of going home.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מוֹמֵי עֲזוּבָה דָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The boy's reply to his uncle's rebuke.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He commits with an oath to stop thinking about leaving.

steps.title: רבי recognizes a familiar voice in his yeshiva
steps.stepSummary: Grown up, the boy sits in רבי's yeshiva, and רבי notices his voice sounds like רבי אלעזר's.
steps.simpleTranslation: When he grew up, he came and sat in רבי's yeshiva. רבי heard his voice and said: This voice sounds like the voice of רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון.
steps.whatsHappening: Years later the boy, now a scholar, learns in רבי's yeshiva, and רבי hears his father in his voice. This sets up the reveal in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story jumps forward to show the rescue succeeded. רבי does not recognize him at first, which shows how much he has changed.

phrases.english: When he grew up, he came and sat
in the academy of Rabbi.
He heard his voice and said:
This voice resembles the voice
of Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי גְדַל אֲתָא יְתֵיב בִּמְתִיבְתָּא דְרַבִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Jumps ahead to show the result of the boy's decision to stay.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The boy has become a scholar learning in רבי's yeshiva.

steps.title: It is his son
steps.stepSummary: The people tell רבי that the speaker is רבי אלעזר's son.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: He is his son.
steps.whatsHappening: The others reveal to רבי that the scholar he heard is the same boy he rescued.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This closes the circle of the story: the wayward son has become a scholar worthy of his father.

phrases.english: They said to him: It is his son.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ: בְּרֵיהּ הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the familiar voice רבי heard in step 19.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The scholar is the son of רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון.

steps.title: רבי applies a פסוק to the son
steps.stepSummary: רבי reads the פסוק from משלי: the fruit of the righteous is a tree of life, and he who wins souls is wise.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי read this פסוק about him: "The fruit of the righteous is a tree of life, and he who wins souls is wise."
steps.whatsHappening: רבי praises what happened by quoting a פסוק that fits the story. The next step explains who each half refers to.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק has two parts, and both fit: a righteous father's "fruit" who became great, and a wise person who "won" a soul back.

keyTerms.meaning: He read a פסוק about him

phrases.english: He read about him:
"The fruit of the righteous is a tree of life,
phrases.notes: משלי 11:30

phrases.english: and he who wins souls is wise."

steps.triggerLanguage: קָרֵי עֲלֵיהּ: ״פְּרִי צַדִּיק עֵץ חַיִּים וְלֹקֵחַ נְפָשׁוֹת חָכָם״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי responds to learning that the scholar is רבי אלעזר's son.
steps.raayaObject: The success of the son and the uncle who taught him.

steps.title: Who each half of the פסוק refers to
steps.stepSummary: The first half refers to רבי יוסי ברבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, and the second half to his uncle רבי שמעון בן איסי בן לקוניא.
steps.simpleTranslation: "The fruit of the righteous is a tree of life" is רבי יוסי ברבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון. "He who wins souls is wise" is רבי שמעון בן איסי בן לקוניא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the פסוק piece by piece, matching each half to a person in the story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The son is the "fruit" of a צדיק who became a source of life himself. The uncle is the wise one who won back a soul by teaching him. Here we learn the son's name for the first time: רבי יוסי.
steps.whatToRemember: The wayward son became רבי יוסי ברבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, and the credit is shared between the son and the uncle who taught him.

phrases.english: "The fruit of the righteous is a tree of life" —

phrases.aramaic: זֶה רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן.
phrases.english: this is Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon.
"And he who wins souls is wise" —

phrases.aramaic: זֶה רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אִיסִי בֶּן לָקוֹנְיָא.
phrases.english: this is Rabbi Shimon ben Isi ben Lakonya.

steps.triggerLanguage: ״פְּרִי צַדִּיק עֵץ חַיִּים״ – זֶה רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the פסוק quoted in step 21.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The first half of the פסוק is the son, רבי יוסי; the second half is his uncle and teacher.

steps.title: A snake surrounds the father's burial cave
steps.stepSummary: When רבי יוסי died, they brought him to his father's cave, but a snake was circling it.
steps.simpleTranslation: When he died, they brought him to his father's cave. A snake was circling around the cave.
steps.whatsHappening: A new scene begins at רבי יוסי's burial: a snake blocks the way into his father's cave. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The family wants to bury the son next to his father, but something blocks it. The story is building toward a question about how the son compares to his father.

phrases.english: When he died,
they brought him to his father's cave.
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets and some the word in square brackets; both mean "they brought him."

phrases.english: A snake was circling around the cave.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי נָח נַפְשֵׁיהּ אַמְטְיוּהּ לִמְעָרְתָּא דַאֲבוּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from רבי יוסי's life to his death and burial.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A snake blocked the entrance to the father's burial cave.

steps.title: They ask the snake to open, but it refuses
steps.stepSummary: They call on the snake to open its mouth so the son can be buried beside his father, but it does not open.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to it: Snake, snake! Open your mouth and let a son come in beside his father. It did not open for them.
steps.whatsHappening: Those at the burial plead with the snake, but it will not let them in.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The snake's refusal is a sign from Heaven that something keeps the son apart from his father. The next step tells us how the people understood it.

phrases.english: He said to it: Snake, snake!
Open your mouth
so that a son may enter beside his father.
It did not open for them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: עַכְנָא עַכְנָא! פְּתַח פִּיךָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The people respond to the snake blocking the cave in step 23.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The snake refused to let the son be buried next to his father.

steps.title: The people conclude the father was greater
steps.stepSummary: The people thought the snake refused because the father was greater than the son.
steps.simpleTranslation: The people thought that this one was greater than that one.
steps.whatsHappening: The people explain the snake's refusal: the father was on a higher level than the son.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word "thought" shows this was the people's understanding of the sign. For now, the story ends with them seeing the father as greater, so the son could not lie beside him.
steps.confusionAlert: The text says the people "thought" this; it describes their assumption, so don't read it as the גמרא's own final word.

phrases.english: The people thought to say
that this one is greater than that one.
phrases.notes: "This one" is the father, רבי אלעזר; "that one" is the son, רבי יוסי.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּסְבוּרִים הָעָם לוֹמַר שֶׁזֶּה גָּדוֹל מִזֶּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the people's explanation for the snake's refusal in step 24.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The people understood the snake's refusal to mean that רבי אלעזר was greater than his son רבי יוסי.

steps.title: A heavenly voice explains the real reason
steps.stepSummary: A בת קול rejects the people's assumption. The snake did not refuse because the father was greater. The father had suffered in the cave and the son had not.
steps.simpleTranslation: A heavenly voice came out and said: It is not because this one is greater than that one. Rather, this one went through the suffering of the cave, and that one did not.
steps.whatsHappening: A voice from heaven corrects what the people thought in the last step. It gives the true reason the snake would not let the son be buried next to his father.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The people assumed the father simply outranked the son in greatness. The בת קול says the son could be just as great. The difference is that the father, רבי אלעזר בן רבי שמעון, suffered for years hiding in a cave, and that suffering earned him a special place.
steps.whatToRemember: The son was kept apart from his father because the father had gone through the suffering of the cave, not because the son was less great.

phrases.english: A heavenly voice came out and said:
Not because this one is greater than that one,
rather, this one went through the suffering of the cave,
phrases.notes: 'This one' is the father, רבי אלעזר בן רבי שמעון, who hid in a cave with his father רבי שמעון.

phrases.english: and that one did not go through the suffering of the cave.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָצְתָה בַּת קוֹל וְאָמְרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the people's explanation from step 25 and gives the true reason.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The people's assumption that the father was greater than the son
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The difference was not greatness. It was that the father had suffered in the cave.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The father's suffering in the cave, not greater stature, is why he had a place his son could not share.

steps.title: רבי asks about רבי טרפון's son
steps.stepSummary: רבי visits רבי טרפון's town and asks whether that צדיק left a son.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי happened to come to רבי טרפון's town. He said to the people: Does that righteous man, who used to swear by the lives of his children, have a son?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new story that is similar to the earlier one. רבי asks whether רבי טרפון has a son, which sets up the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just as רבי looked after רבי אלעזר's son earlier, he now looks for רבי טרפון's family. He describes רבי טרפון as the צדיק who used to swear by the lives of his children.

keyTerms.meaning: Swore by the lives of his children

phrases.english: Rebbi happened to come to the town of Rabbi Tarfon.
He said to them:
Does that righteous man have a son,
the one who used to swear by the lives of his children?
phrases.notes: Literally 'who would cut off his children.' He used to take oaths on his children's lives.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיקְּלַע רַבִּי לְאַתְרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי טַרְפוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new, similar story about רבי caring for a great man's descendant.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רבי טרפון has a son.

steps.title: The people describe a wayward grandson
steps.stepSummary: The townspeople answer that רבי טרפון has no son. He has a grandson, his daughter's son, who is living a very immoral life.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: He has no son, but he has a daughter's son, and every prostitute who is hired for two coins hires him for eight.
steps.whatsHappening: The people answer רבי's question. They tell him about רבי טרפון's grandson and how far he has fallen.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is no son, but there is a grandson through his daughter. The strange picture of prostitutes paying him shows how deeply he was caught up in immoral living.

phrases.english: They said to him: A son he does not have;
a daughter's son he does have,
and every prostitute who is hired for two coins
hires him for eight.
phrases.notes: A way of saying he was deep into an immoral life.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: בֵּן אֵין לוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי's question from step 27.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No son, but a grandson who is living immorally.

steps.title: רבי offers his daughter and the grandson repents
steps.stepSummary: The grandson is brought to רבי. רבי promises him his daughter if he repents, and he does.
steps.simpleTranslation: They brought him before רבי. רבי said to him: If you repent, I will give you my daughter. He repented.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי meets the grandson and makes him an offer: do תשובה and you can marry my daughter. The grandson repents.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי does not just scold the young man. He offers him a great honor, marrying into the נשיא's family, to pull him back to a good path. The plan works.

phrases.english: They brought him before Rebbi.
He said to him:
If you repent,
I will give you my daughter.
He repented.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַתְיוּהּ לְקַמֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story: רבי acts on what he heard.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי brought the grandson to תשובה by offering him his daughter.

steps.title: Two versions of whether he married her
steps.stepSummary: Some say the grandson married רבי's daughter and later divorced her. Others say he never married her, so no one would think he repented only to win her.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: He married her and divorced her. Others say: He did not marry her at all, so that people would not say he repented only for her sake.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives two opinions about how the story ended. The question is whether the grandson actually married רבי's daughter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The second version explains why he would refuse such an honor. He wanted it to be clear that his תשובה was sincere and not a bargain to win a wife.

phrases.english: Some say: He married her and divorced her.
Some say: He did not marry her at all,
so that people would not say
that this man repented for the sake of this woman.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי: נַסְבַהּ וְגָירְשַׁהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds two versions of how the story ended.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There are two versions: he married and divorced her, or he never married her so his תשובה would look sincere.

steps.title: Why did רבי go to so much trouble?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי put in so much effort to bring these young men back.
steps.simpleTranslation: And why did he need all this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops and asks a question about the stories it just told. Why did רבי work so hard? This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי went to great lengths, even offering his own daughter, to rescue these wayward descendants. The גמרא wants to know what drove him to do so much.

phrases.english: And why did he need all this?
phrases.notes: He means all of רבי's effort to bring these young men back to תורה.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְמָה לֵיהּ כּוּלֵּי הַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the reason behind רבי's actions in the stories.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רבי worked so hard to bring these young men back.

steps.title: Teaching a friend's son earns a seat in heaven
steps.stepSummary: The answer, given in the name of three chains of teachers: whoever teaches תורה to his friend's son earns a seat in the heavenly ישיבה. The proof comes from a פסוק in ירמיהו.
steps.simpleTranslation: For רב יהודה said in the name of רב, and some say רבי חייא בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן, and some say רבי שמואל בר נחמני said in the name of רבי יונתן: Anyone who teaches תורה to his friend's son merits to sit in the heavenly ישיבה, as it says: 'If you return, and I bring you back, you shall stand before Me.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. רבי worked so hard because teaching תורה to someone else's child brings a huge reward in the next world.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The teaching is reported in three different ways, but all three versions say the same thing. The פסוק says that one who brings others back to ה׳ will stand before Him, which is read as sitting in the heavenly ישיבה.
steps.whatToRemember: Teaching תורה to another person's child earns a seat in the heavenly ישיבה. That is why רבי worked so hard to bring these young men back.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains the whole set of stories. It shows how highly the גמרא values bringing others, especially the children of others, to תורה.

phrases.english: For Rav Yehuda said in the name of Rav,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרִי לַהּ אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן,
phrases.english: and some say Rabbi Chiya bar Abba said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרִי לַהּ אָמַר רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹנָתָן:
phrases.english: and some say Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani said in the name of Rabbi Yonatan:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל הַמְלַמֵּד אֶת בֶּן חֲבֵירוֹ תּוֹרָה
phrases.english: Anyone who teaches Torah to his friend's son
merits to sit in the heavenly yeshiva,
as it is said:
"If you return, and I bring you back, you shall stand before Me."
phrases.notes: ירמיהו 15:19

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 31 with a teaching and a פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Whoever teaches Torah to his friend's son earns a seat in the heavenly ישיבה, based on ירמיהו 15:19.

steps.title: Teaching the son of an unlearned man can cancel a heavenly decree
steps.stepSummary: Whoever teaches תורה to the son of an עם הארץ is so precious that even a decree of הקדוש ברוך הוא can be canceled for his sake. The proof is a פסוק in ירמיהו.
steps.simpleTranslation: And anyone who teaches תורה to the son of an unlearned person: even if הקדוש ברוך הוא makes a decree, He cancels it for his sake, as it says: 'If you bring out the precious from the worthless, you will be like My mouth.'
steps.whatsHappening: The same teaching from the last step keeps going and adds a second, even bigger reward. Teaching a friend's son earns a seat in heaven. For someone who teaches the son of an עם הארץ, הקדוש ברוך הוא cancels His own decrees for that teacher's sake.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 32 spoke about teaching your friend's son. Here the case is harder: the boy's father is an עם הארץ, so the teacher is bringing out something precious from a place with no תורה. The words 'like My mouth' are read to mean that this teacher's word has power like ה׳'s own word, strong enough to cancel a decree.

keyTerms.meaning: An unlearned person who does not know תורה
The Holy One, Blessed be He (ה׳)
A decree, here a harsh decree from heaven
You will be like My mouth

phrases.aramaic: וְכׇל הַמְלַמֵּד אֶת בֶּן עַם הָאָרֶץ תּוֹרָה –
phrases.english: And anyone who teaches Torah to the son of an unlearned person —

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא גּוֹזֵר גְּזֵירָה,
phrases.english: even if the Holy One, Blessed be He, issues a decree,
He cancels it for his sake,
as it is said:
"And if you bring out the precious from the worthless, you shall be like My mouth."
phrases.notes: ירמיהו 15:19. This is the same פסוק as before; this time the גמרא uses its ending, 'like My mouth.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכׇל הַמְלַמֵּד אֶת בֶּן עַם הָאָרֶץ תּוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same statement from step 32 and adds a second, greater level of reward.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Teaching תורה to the son of an עם הארץ gives a person such merit that ה׳ cancels decrees for him.

steps.title: Three generations of scholars means תורה stays in the family forever
steps.stepSummary: רבי פרנך, quoting רבי יוחנן, teaches that if a man, his son, and his grandson are all תלמידי חכמים, תורה will never leave his descendants. The proof is a פסוק in ישעיהו that names three generations.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי פרנך said in the name of רבי יוחנן: Anyone who is a תלמיד חכם, and his son is a תלמיד חכם, and his grandson is a תלמיד חכם, תורה will never again stop from his descendants, as it says: 'And as for Me, this is My covenant... they will not leave your mouth, or the mouth of your children, or the mouth of your children's children, says ה׳, from now and forever.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching about תלמידי חכמים and their families. Three generations in a row of תורה scholars brings a promise that תורה will stay in that family forever.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק lists three mouths: yours, your children's, and your grandchildren's. Then it adds 'from now and forever.' רבי יוחנן reads this to mean that once three generations have learned, the promise covers every generation after that.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי פַּרְנָךְ אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Parnakh said in the name of Rabbi Yoḥanan:
Anyone who is a Torah scholar,
and his son is a Torah scholar,
and his grandson is a Torah scholar —

phrases.aramaic: שׁוּב אֵין תּוֹרָה פּוֹסֶקֶת מִזַּרְעוֹ לְעוֹלָם,
phrases.english: the Torah will never again stop from his descendants,
as it is said: "And as for Me, this is My covenant, etc.
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 59:21. 'וגו׳' means 'and so on': the גמרא skips the middle of the פסוק.

phrases.english: they shall not leave your mouth, nor the mouth of your children,
nor the mouth of your children's children,
says the Lord, from now and forever."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי פַּרְנָךְ אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the reward for teaching others to a related idea: תורה lasting inside one's own family.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If three generations in a row are תלמידי חכמים, תורה will never leave that family.

steps.title: Why does the verse say 'says ה׳'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the words 'says ה׳' add to the פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is meant by 'says ה׳'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to ask about one phrase in the פסוק. This question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The whole פסוק is already ה׳ speaking, so the words 'says ה׳' seem extra. The גמרא wants to know what these extra words teach.

phrases.english: What is meant by "says the Lord"?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי ״אָמַר ה׳״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about a phrase in the פסוק just quoted in step 34.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the extra words 'says ה׳' add to the promise.

steps.title: ה׳ personally guarantees the promise
steps.stepSummary: The words 'says ה׳' mean that הקדוש ברוך הוא Himself stands as guarantor for this promise.
steps.simpleTranslation: הקדוש ברוך הוא said: I am your guarantor in this matter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 35. The words 'says ה׳' show that ה׳ Himself guarantees this promise.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An ערב is someone who personally promises that a deal will be kept. The extra words turn the פסוק into ה׳'s personal guarantee that תורה will stay in the family.

keyTerms.meaning: A guarantor, someone who personally backs a promise

phrases.english: The Holy One, Blessed be He, said:
I am your guarantor in this matter.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא: אֲנִי עָרֵב לְךָ בְּדָבָר זֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 35.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'Says ה׳' means ה׳ personally guarantees the promise.

steps.title: What does 'from now and forever' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks about a second phrase in the פסוק: 'from now and forever.'
steps.simpleTranslation: What is meant by 'from now and forever'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks about another phrase in the same פסוק. This sets up רבי ירמיה's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק names only three generations, yet it ends with 'forever.' The גמרא wants to know how 'forever' fits with a list of just three.

phrases.english: What is meant by "from now and forever"?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי ״מֵעַתָּה וְעַד עוֹלָם״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second question about the same פסוק, parallel to step 35.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the words 'forever' relate to the three generations named in the פסוק.

steps.title: After three generations, תורה returns to its home
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה explains that after three generations, תורה keeps coming back to that family, like a guest returning to the inn where it always stays.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה said: From here on, תורה returns to its lodging place.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה answers the question from step 37. Once three generations have learned, the family becomes תורה's regular home.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'From now' means from the point after three generations. From then on, תורה is like a traveler who always comes back to the same inn, so it keeps coming back to this family 'forever.'
steps.whatToRemember: Three generations of תלמידי חכמים make the family a permanent 'home' for תורה, and ה׳ Himself guarantees it.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya said:
From here on,
the Torah returns to its lodging place.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה: מִכָּאן וְאֵילָךְ תּוֹרָה מְחַזֶּרֶת עַל אַכְסַנְיָא שֶׁלָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 37.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: After three generations, תורה keeps returning to that family as its permanent home.

steps.title: רב יוסף fasts until he is shown the full promise
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף fasted forty fasts and was shown the first part of the פסוק. After forty more he was shown the second part. After another round of fasts he was shown the full promise covering three generations.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף fasted forty fasts, and they had him read 'They will not leave your mouth.' He fasted forty more fasts, and they had him read 'They will not leave your mouth or the mouth of your children.' He fasted another forty (some versions: one hundred) fasts, and they had him read 'They will not leave your mouth, or the mouth of your children, or the mouth of your children's children.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story that shows the teaching of רבי יוחנן in action. רב יוסף fasted in rounds, and after each round he was shown more of the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each round of fasting added one more generation to the promise: first himself, then his children, then his grandchildren. This matches the three generations in the פסוק exactly.

keyTerms.meaning: Sat (here: sat in fasting, meaning he fasted)
They had him read, he was shown

phrases.english: Rav Yosef fasted forty fasts,
and they had him read: "They shall not leave your mouth."
He fasted forty more fasts,
and they had him read: "They shall not leave your mouth, nor the mouth of your children."
He fasted another (one hundred) [forty] fasts,
phrases.notes: The printed גמרא says 'one hundred' in round brackets. The corrected wording, in square brackets, says 'forty'.

phrases.english: and they had him read: "They shall not leave your mouth, nor the mouth of your children,
nor the mouth of your children's children."

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב יוֹסֵף יְתֵיב אַרְבְּעִין תַּעֲנִיָּתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A story showing the three-generation promise of steps 34 and 38 in a real person's life.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב יוסף fasted round after round until he was shown the promise covering three generations of his family.

steps.title: רב יוסף stops fasting, sure that תורה will stay in his family
steps.stepSummary: After seeing the full promise, רב יוסף says he no longer needs to fast, because from now on תורה will return to its home in his family.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said: From here on I do not need to fast. תורה returns to its lodging place.
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends. רב יוסף uses רבי ירמיה's exact words to explain why he can stop fasting.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once he was shown three generations, he did not need to ask for a fourth. By רבי ירמיה's teaching, three generations already make the family תורה's permanent home.

keyTerms.meaning: I do not need to (fast anymore)

steps.whatToRemember: רב יוסף's story proves רבי ירמיה's point: once three generations are covered, תורה stays in the family forever, so there is nothing more to ask for.

phrases.english: He said: From here on I do not need [to fast] —
the Torah returns to its lodging place.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר: מִכָּאן וְאֵילָךְ לָא צְרִיכְנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the story of step 39 using the teaching of רבי ירמיה from step 38.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Three generations of תורה are enough. After that, תורה keeps returning to the family by itself.

steps.title: רבי זירא's three hundred fasts
steps.stepSummary: When רבי זירא moved to ארץ ישראל, he fasted three rounds of one hundred fasts, each for a different goal.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבי זירא went up to ארץ ישראל, he fasted one hundred fasts so he would forget the Babylonian way of learning, so it would not get in his way. He fasted another hundred so that רבי אלעזר would not die during his lifetime, which would have put the community's burdens on him. And he fasted another hundred so that the fire of גיהנם would not have power over him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story about רבי זירא that is similar to רב יוסף's fasts. He fasted three sets of one hundred fasts, each with its own purpose.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like רב יוסף, רבי זירא used fasting to ask for something connected to his learning. The first goal was to forget the Babylonian style so he could learn the way they learned in ארץ ישראל. The second goal was that רבי אלעזר would stay alive and keep handling the community, so רבי זירא could keep learning. The third goal was to be protected from גיהנם.

keyTerms.meaning: The Babylonian way of learning גמרא

steps.confusionAlert: He did not fast to forget Torah. He fasted to forget the Babylonian method of learning, so he could take on the style of ארץ ישראל.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי זֵירָא כִּי סְלֵיק לְאַרְעָא דְיִשְׂרָאֵל
phrases.english: When Rabbi Zeira went up to Eretz Yisrael
he sat one hundred fasts
phrases.notes: To 'sit' a fast just means to keep it. He fasted a hundred times.

phrases.english: so that the Babylonian way of learning would be forgotten from him,
so that it would not get in his way.
He fasted another hundred
so that Rabbi Elazar would not die in his years,
phrases.notes: Literally 'lie down,' meaning die. 'In his years' means during רבי זירא's lifetime.

phrases.english: and then the community's matters would fall on him.
And he fasted another hundred,
so that the fire of Gehinnom would not have power over him.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי זֵירָא כִּי סְלֵיק לְאַרְעָא דְיִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel story to רב יוסף's fasts: another אמורא who fasted for goals connected to his תורה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי זירא fasted 300 fasts: to forget the Babylonian learning style, for רבי אלעזר's long life, and for protection from גיהנם.

steps.title: רבי זירא tests himself in the oven
steps.stepSummary: Every thirty days רבי זירא sat inside a burning oven to check that his protection still worked. One day the רבנן's envious eye caused his legs to be singed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Every thirty days he would test himself. He would heat up an oven, climb in, and sit inside it, and the fire would not affect him. One day the רבנן put an eye on him, and his legs got singed. From then on they called him 'the short one with singed legs.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues the רבי זירא story. It shows how he checked that his third goal, protection from fire, had really worked.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The oven test showed that his fasts had worked: fire had no power over him. The one time it failed was because of עין הרע, the envious eye of the רבנן. Even then, only his legs were burned. The nickname comes from that day.

keyTerms.meaning: They put an (envious) eye on him; עין הרע
The short one with singed legs (his nickname)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי זירא's fasts are a second example, after רב יוסף, of a great חכם who fasted for spiritual goals and was answered.

phrases.english: Every thirty days
he would test himself:
he would heat an oven, climb in, and sit inside it
and the fire would not affect him.

phrases.aramaic: יוֹמָא חַד יְהַבוּ בֵּיהּ רַבָּנַן עֵינָא
phrases.english: One day the Rabbis put an eye on him
phrases.notes: An 'eye' here means an envious look, what we call עין הרע.

phrases.english: and his legs got singed,
and they called him 'the short one with singed legs.'

steps.triggerLanguage: כֹּל תְּלָתִין יוֹמֵי הֲוָה בָּדֵיק נַפְשֵׁיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows how רבי זירא confirmed that his third set of fasts, for protection from fire, had worked.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Fire did not harm רבי זירא, except once, when the רבנן's envious eye caused his legs to be singed.

steps.title: רב begins explaining the verse about why the land was lost
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה, quoting רב, asks what a פסוק in ירמיה means: who is wise enough to explain why the land was destroyed? He begins his answer with 'This matter...'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: What is the meaning of the פסוק, 'Who is the wise man who can understand this, and to whom has the mouth of ה׳ spoken, so that he can tell it: why was the land lost?' This matter...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new teaching about תורה study. רב asks what a פסוק means, and he is setting up an explanation that continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק asks a question: why was the land destroyed? It suggests that wise men and even נביאים could not answer it. רב is about to explain that this question was so hard that no one could figure it out until ה׳ Himself explained it. The words 'דבר זה' are the first words of that explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the meaning of what is written? (a phrase that opens the explanation of a פסוק)

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said in the name of Rav:
What is the meaning of what is written:
'Who is the wise man, who can understand this,
phrases.notes: ירמיהו 9:11

phrases.aramaic: וַאֲשֶׁר דִּבֶּר פִּי ה׳ אֵלָיו וְיַגִּדָהּ
phrases.english: and to whom has the mouth of ה׳ spoken, so he can tell it:
why was the land lost?'
This matter...
phrases.notes: This is the start of רב's answer. The sentence finishes on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב: מַאי דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from stories about fasting for תורה to a new teaching about תורה study and the destruction of the land.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב sets out to explain the פסוק's question about why the land was destroyed. The explanation continues on the next amud.
